strings.d1.s0.name: Jaffa Port
strings.d1.s0.tips: A 4,000-year-old harbour with fishing boats and the Tel Aviv skyline, best in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Old Jaffa Kedumim Square
strings.d1.s1.tips: Stone lanes, St Peter's Church, the Zodiac alleys and the Hanging Orange Tree.
strings.d1.s2.name: Abu Hassan Ali Karavan
strings.d1.s2.tips: Israel's most famous hummus, served for 50 years. Come before noon (it closes when it sells out); tables are shared.
strings.d1.s3.name: Jaffa Flea Market Shuk HaPishpeshim
strings.d1.s3.tips: Antiques, vintage and design. Open Sunday to Thursday, closes at 14:00 on Friday; plenty of cafés.
strings.d1.s4.name: Jaffa Beach & Charles Clore Park
strings.d1.s4.tips: Walk the seafront from Jaffa to Tel Aviv at sunset.
strings.d1.b0.name: Dr. Shakshuka
strings.d1.b0.tips: Libyan-style shakshuka; opens at 08:00, in Jaffa.
strings.d1.b1.name: Ilana Goor Museum
strings.d1.b1.tips: The artist's 18th-century house-museum, with sea views from the roof.
strings.d2.theme: Carmel Market and the White City
strings.d2.s0.name: Carmel Market
strings.d2.s0.tips: The city's biggest market: sabich, halva and fresh juice. Liveliest on Friday.
strings.d2.s1.name: Rothschild Boulevard
strings.d2.s1.tips: The Bauhaus boulevard of UNESCO's White City, with Independence Hall (1948) and kiosk cafés.
strings.d2.s2.name: Bauhaus Center Tel Aviv
strings.d2.s2.tips: Based on Dizengoff: a map of 4,000 Bauhaus buildings and a Friday tour.
strings.d2.s3.name: Miznon Ibn Gabirol
strings.d2.s3.tips: Eyal Shani's pita shop. Try the whole cauliflower, eaten on the street.
strings.d2.s4.name: Dizengoff Square
strings.d2.s4.tips: Agam's Fire and Water fountain, with cafés around it.
strings.d2.b0.name: Port Sa'id
strings.d2.b0.tips: A stylish restaurant opposite the Great Synagogue; records and meze.
strings.d2.b1.name: Independence Hall
strings.d2.b1.tips: The hall where the Declaration of Independence was read; book ahead.
strings.d3.s0.name: Gordon Beach
strings.d3.s0.tips: The city beach: the clack of matkot paddles, sunrise swims, sun loungers 15 ILS.
strings.d3.s1.name: Tel Aviv Port Namal
strings.d3.s1.tips: A wooden boardwalk in the old port; Friday farmers' market.
strings.d3.s2.name: Shuk HaNamal Port Market
strings.d3.s2.tips: An indoor gourmet market with fish and cheese.
strings.d3.s3.name: Yarkon Park
strings.d3.s3.tips: The city's Central Park: cycling, rowing boats and a tropical garden.
strings.d3.s4.name: Banana Beach Sunset
strings.d3.s4.tips: A beach bar and a Mediterranean sunset.
strings.d3.b0.name: Benedict Ben Yehuda
strings.d3.b1.name: Hilton Beach
strings.d3.b1.tips: A gay-friendly surf beach; an alternative to Gordon.
strings.d4.s0.name: Neve Tzedek
strings.d4.s0.tips: The first neighbourhood, founded in 1887: Shabazi Street boutiques and the Suzanne Dellal dance centre.
strings.d4.s1.name: Dallal Bakery
strings.d4.s1.tips: A bakery-café in Neve Tzedek; try the croissant.
strings.d4.s2.name: Florentin Street Art
strings.d4.s2.tips: The graffiti neighbourhood; spices at Levinsky Market.
strings.d4.s3.name: Levinsky Market Café Levinsky 41
strings.d4.s3.tips: Gazoz (homemade fruit soda) and the spice market; Balkan burek.
strings.d4.s4.name: Sarona Market
strings.d4.s4.tips: A gourmet market in the German Templer colony; Anita ice cream.
strings.d4.b0.name: Nahalat Binyamin Bar Evening Teder
strings.d4.b0.tips: A courtyard bar-radio; Florentin at night.
strings.d4.b1.name: Nahum Gutman Museum
strings.d4.b1.tips: The Neve Tzedek painter; an alternative to Florentin.
strings.d5.s0.name: Caesarea National Park
strings.d5.s0.tips: 45 minutes by train plus a bus or tour. Herod's Roman harbour, hippodrome and theatre, and the aqueduct beach.
strings.d5.s1.name: Bahá'í Gardens Haifa
strings.d5.s1.tips: UNESCO's 19-terrace gardens on Mount Carmel. The view from the upper entrance is free (guided tour at 12:00); the German Colony lies below.
strings.d5.s2.name: Haifa German Colony Fattoush
strings.d5.s2.tips: Meze in the Arab-Christian quarter along Ben Gurion Boulevard.
strings.d5.s3.name: Acre Old City
strings.d5.s3.tips: The Crusader underground city (Hospitaller fortress 50 ILS), the Ottoman market and port, and the Turkish bath museum.
strings.d5.s4.name: Uri Buri Acre
strings.d5.s4.tips: A world-famous fish restaurant; booking essential. Then the train back.
strings.d5.b0.name: Hummus Said Acre
strings.d5.b0.tips: Legendary hummus in the Acre market; it sells out by noon.
strings.d5.b1.name: Rosh Hanikra
strings.d5.b1.tips: A cable car to sea caves on the Lebanese border; an alternative to Acre.
strings.d6.s0.name: Tel Aviv Museum of Art
strings.d6.s0.tips: A building like broken crystal; Israeli and modern art, Lichtenstein, free on Tuesday evening.
strings.d6.s1.name: ANU Museum of the Jewish People
strings.d6.s1.tips: The Diaspora museum at Tel Aviv University; interactive.
strings.d6.s2.name: HaKosem Falafel
strings.d6.s2.tips: The city's best falafel and sabich, on Shlomo HaMelech.
strings.d6.s3.name: Ben Gurion House
strings.d6.s3.tips: The prime minister's home and his 20,000 books; free.
strings.d6.s4.name: Shabbat Dinner Ha'achim
strings.d6.s4.tips: Restaurants fill up on Friday evening; charcoal grill, book ahead.
strings.d6.b0.name: Eretz Israel Museum
strings.d6.b0.tips: Archaeology and glass; next to the ANU.
strings.d6.b1.name: Dizengoff Center Food Market
strings.d6.b1.tips: A food market inside the mall, Thursday and Friday.
strings.d7.theme: Morning on the beach, a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Frishman Beach Morning
strings.d7.s0.tips: Swim or run in the morning; the beach is empty.
strings.d7.s1.name: Café Xoho
strings.d7.s2.name: Ben Yehuda Street Souvenirs
strings.d7.s2.tips: Dead Sea cosmetics and tahini to take home.
strings.d7.s3.name: HaHagana Train Ben Gurion
strings.d7.s3.tips: The train to the airport takes 15 minutes (none on Shabbat; on Saturday a taxi costs 150 ILS). Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Bucke Cafe Ben Yehuda
strings.d7.b1.name: Sarona Gardens Morning
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Templer garden; an alternative to souvenir shopping.
strings.note0: Use a Rav-Kav card for buses and light rail (since 2023); bikes and scooters are everywhere. The airport train takes 15 minutes (it does NOT run on Shabbat, from Friday evening to Saturday evening, so take a taxi). Trains run to Haifa.
strings.note1: Summer is 30-33°C with 70% humidity. Go to the beach at sunrise or sunset and to museums at midday. Pride is in June and August is the most humid.
strings.note2: SAFETY: The regional situation is changeable. Check official travel advice, use the Home Front Command app and follow shelter instructions.
strings.note3: Hummus 35-50 ILS, falafel 20-25, breakfast 50-70, restaurant meal 120-180. It is an expensive city; tip 12-15% (cash preferred). Cards are accepted everywhere.
strings.note4: Shabbat: from Friday sunset to Saturday evening most places close, but the beach, Jaffa and restaurants stay open. Markets are liveliest on Friday morning.
strings.note5: Buses 405 and 480 reach Jerusalem in 1 hour (not on Shabbat); a day trip is possible.
